newsitem.title: USA: Noel sells 9 percent of HealthPlan stock.
newsitem.headline: Noel sells 9 percent of HealthPlan stock.

text.p: Noel Group Inc. said Friday it sold 1.32 million shares of HealthPlan Services Corp., a 9 percent stake in the health care services company, to Automatic Data Processing Inc. for $20 a share, or $26.4 million.
Noel, a New York-based holding company for small and medium-sized companies, said the sale cut its stake in HealthPlan to about 29 percent.
HealthPlan, based in Tampa, Fla., provides distribution, enrollment, billing and collection and claims administration for health care payors and providers.
Under the agreement, Automatic Data, which provides computing services, cannot acquire additional HealthPlan shares during a specified period so as not to raise the stake to above 10 percent.
The deal also prohibits Automatic Data, based in Roseland, N.J., from taking any action to seek control of HealthPlan, unless approved by the HealthPlan board, Noel said.
Noel said that, other than a distribution to Noel shareholders, it has agreed not to transfer its remaining shares in HealthPlan before Sept. 30.
HealthPlan's stock fell 25 cents to $22.125, while Automatic Data rose 37.5 cents to $42.125 on the New York Stock Exchange. Noel was unchanged at $7.125 on Nasdaq.
